findings.title: Shared default timestamp for all instances
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18, `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` once at import time. Every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` shares the same timestamp. The field no longer reflects when the assignment was queued, breaking debugging, ordering, and any future staleness/TTL logic. Fix with `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: to_dict returns non-JSON-serializable datetime for Celery
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py `to_dict` returns `asdict(self)` containing a raw `datetime` for `queued`. Callers in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` pass this dict as `assignment_source_dict` to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` kwargs, which must survive Celery serialization. With JSON serialization this raises a serialization error and outbound sync fails/retries; after a JSON round-trip `queued` comes back as a string, violating the declared `datetime` type. Serialize `queued` to ISO format and parse it back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: from_dict accepts wrong types and defeats cycle check
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py `from_dict` does `cls(**input_dict)` and only catches ValueError/TypeError. A dict like `{'source_name': 'x', 'integration_id': '123', 'queued': '2024-...'}` succeeds but yields `integration_id` as str and `queued` as str. Later `should_sync` checks `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` where the latter is int, so int vs str is False and same-integration suppression silently fails, reintroducing the sync loop. Validate/coerce types and return None on mismatch.

findings.title: Corrupt source fails open and reintroduces loop
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py the task does `AssignmentSource.from_dict(...) if assignment_source_dict else None` and then calls `should_sync(..., parsed_source)`. If `from_dict` returns None due to corrupt/extra/missing keys, the code proceeds with None, which `should_sync` treats as no source and returns True, so it syncs outbound anyway. A malformed payload therefore disables the cycle protection this PR adds and resumes the loop. It should skip/log and return instead of failing open.

findings.title: sync_assignee_outbound contract missing assignment_source
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py the abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` is declared as `(external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs)` with no explicit `assignment_source`, yet `sync_assignee_outbound` task calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_source)` and tests assert it is passed explicitly. Any concrete integration implementing the strict 3-arg signature without `**kwargs` will raise TypeError at runtime, and with `**kwargs` the value is silently swallowed. Add the explicit `assignment_source` parameter to the abstract as done for `sync_status_outbound`.
